newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sells state holdings for $18.5 million.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sells state holdings for $18.5 million.

text.p: Algeria has carried out 26 sales in its privatisation programme this year, in which seven share transfers had brought the treasury more than one billion dinars ($18.5 million), the Algerian cabinet said on Wednesday.
In a statement after the weekly meeting, carried by the official news agency APS, the ministers said among these operations was the sale of the Chateauneuf Hotel in the western city of Oran.

The sum involved here was over 500 million dinars (($9.25 million). The hotel, put up for sale in 1994, had "been the object of a positive submission by a national private operator", the cabinet said, adding that it had given its agreement to the transfer.
It gave no other details other than to say that six other share transfer operations "which had more modest values" had been carried out on the basis of tenders opened under the official supervision.

Privatisation is a contentious issue in Algeria, with local and foreign economists urging the rapid sale of state-owned companies in a drive to modernise them, and many officials fearing mass lay-offs would inevitably follow and fuel social unrest.

The country has already lived through nearly five years of violence in which about 50,000 people have died, and officials say poverty and lack of jobs or hope drove many young people into the ranks of armed Moslem fundamentalists.
Algeria has so far adopted at least three systems of privatisation -- share transfers, management buyouts, and complete sale to an outside investor.

President Liamine Zeroual earlier this month expressed dismay at the slow pace of privatisation. World Bank experts have called for mass privatisation of around 1,350 enterprises seen as saleable, including one suggesting "privatisation sale by vouchers".

But on Tuesday, the man appointed to oversee privatisation, Abderrahmane Mebtoul, said it would be carried out "case by case...with the aim of avoiding social unheaval jeopardising all the reform process."
